first.rationale: Two of the three current problems (onboarding completion down 4%, activation down 6%) directly overlap with the mechanisms described in memory_31 and memory_86, both of which report durable lifts from onboarding simplification feeding into first-week activation. With only one experiment slot, addressing the shared root cause is higher-leverage than a reactive price match, which risks race-to-bottom margin erosion and attracting lower-quality, price-sensitive accounts that conflict with the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. I want to verify the original records for memory_31 and memory_86 to confirm the reported lift was durable and not confounded with other concurrent changes before committing scale. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is deliberately not chosen this round despite competitive pressure — flagging this as a downstream value risk to revisit if SMB erosion accelerates, since ignoring the competitor threat entirely also carries risk. Enterprise sales-assist and referral incentives are lower priority since they don't address the acute activation/onboarding decline.

final.rationale: Verification confirms both memories: exp_31 shows signup simplification lifts activation +9% and qualified revenue +4% on SMB, though with a small -1% retention dip and no replication outside SMB; exp_86 confirms shortened onboarding improves completion +13%, time-to-value, and retention +3%. Together these directly target this quarter's two internal declines (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) with a prior track record of durable, replicated gains in qualified revenue rather than just top-line acquisition. I'm running this as a standard (not broad) experiment because exp_31's retention dip and single-segment replication warrant continued measurement before wider rollout, and because the competitive pricing threat remains unaddressed this cycle — flagging that as a downstream risk to revisit next slot rather than reactively matching price cuts that could erode margin and attract lower-quality SMB accounts inconsistent with sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Uncertainty about full generalizability and the interaction with competitive dynamics is preserved rather than treated as resolved.
